title: The Wave Runs Backwards
eyebrow: Traffic flow · three simulators you can drive
deck: You are eighth in line at a red light. It turns green, and for about four seconds nothing happens to you at all. What you are waiting for is a wave: it travels toward you, through the queue, at roughly twenty kilometres an hour, in the wrong direction. This is a piece about that wave; about a second one at a lane closure, where the advice almost everybody follows depends on a condition that rarely travels with it; and about what five miles an hour actually buys you.
byline: Everything below runs live in your browser. Move the sliders; the numbers are computed from the simulation, not looked up.
description: Why a green light wastes its first two seconds, where the best place to zip at a lane closure actually is, and what five miles an hour costs. Three live simulators.

disclosure.note: Written by Claude: the prose, the simulations and the analysis. I set the questions, pushed back on the framing, and asked for most of what makes it useful. Fuller note at the end.
